changelog:
Three faults found by running 1.0.77.0 and 1.0.78.0 against a real server and looking at the page, and one change to what a longer schedule is for. **Asking what a schedule edit would do changed the schedule.** The rehearsal that draws your pending edits before you save them was walking the channel's live week rather than a copy of it - so asking "what would this come to" left the channel changed, on air, with nothing written to disk. A restart undid it, which is exactly how it could have gone unnoticed. It works on a copy now, and four tests check the week it was asked about is untouched afterwards, which is a thing no test here was checking. **And a schedule longer than a week could be destroyed by saving it**: the write path tidied every week against a length of exactly seven days, so anything in a second week would have been folded on top of the first.

**A schedule can now be made as long as its content.** That is what the setting is for: a channel of every episode of a series should air all of them and then start again, and a week-long schedule airs the first week's worth for ever and never reaches the rest - with nothing anywhere saying so, because a week of it looks perfectly right. A button works out how long the channel takes to play everything once, makes the schedule that long and lays it out. Typing a number still works; nobody knew what the number was.

The rest: the band of empty space below the page came back, because the fix for the scroll bar reacted to the page overflowing rather than measuring what is actually below the app - anything else on the page that overflowed took height away from this one. Both ends are measured now. The picture gallery's shape filters named none of the three pictures a channel wears: they say what they give now, pressing Change picks the right one for that slot, and the banner - which no provider anywhere serves - says so instead of leaving you to work out why it is missing. And the gallery's heading no longer jumps about when you select something: a line of text that changes length was re-wrapping the row it sits in and moving every control with it.
description: Lightweight virtual TV channels: deterministic schedules over your own library, tuned in via normal direct playback at the live position. No transcoding, no tuner emulation.
name: LiteTV Channels
overview: TV channels from your library, without transcoding.
